rows.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (EMEA)
rows.eligibility: Tier 1 - posting states remote within the EMEA region and quotes the band in EUR, so an Italy-resident hire is in scope; note the JD also carries a boilerplate US-visa sentence ('unable to sponsor employment visas') that contradicts the EMEA framing - worth one clarifying question but the location field and EUR comp both say EMEA
rows.comp: EUR 100,000 - EUR 135,000 (band spans career levels, narrowed at interview)
rows.posted: not disclosed on posting (Greenhouse renders no date; role was live when fetched 2026-08-05)
rows.why: The only mid-band FDE in the slice with an explicit EMEA-remote location and a disclosed EUR salary: 3+ years required against his ~3, and the job is sitting in sales meetings giving architectural guidance then unblocking escalated customer issues, which is exactly the client-facing delivery pattern he ran across FlowSpace, Urlink, Qomodo and Clubee. His API-integration depth (Office RnD, Nexudus, CRM lead capture, Sendgrid, OpenAI) and habit of writing technical docs and training material map straight onto the documentation and enablement half of the role.
rows.watch_outs: GPU-cloud infrastructure company, so the troubleshooting surface is Linux/Ubuntu, Docker, TCP/IP, SSH and DNS rather than product logic - that is the thinnest part of his CV. Go is 'preferred' and he has none. The contradictory US-visa boilerplate needs clearing before he invests in the application. No posted date exposed, so freshness is unconfirmed.

rows.title: Technical Product Manager
rows.eligibility: Tier 1 - the posting's location statement is 'Remote in Europe' with no country allow-list and no work-authorisation carve-out, so his EU long-term residence permit covers it from Venice
rows.posted: not disclosed on posting (EU Greenhouse renders no date; live when fetched 2026-08-05)
rows.why: States no year count, which per his profile is the friendliest shape of TPM posting for someone with ~3 years and a Lead Developer title rather than a PM one. The core loop - sit with technical users, turn their pain into specs, own roadmap through delivery, coordinate design and engineering - is what he actually did at FlowSpace, where he wrote the business-logic documentation, mediated between the internal team and an external agency, and owned QA while taking the product from 2,000 to 4,500+ users.
rows.watch_outs: Users are AI/ML researchers doing model training and experiment tracking; he is an applied LLM/agent builder, not a trainer, so the domain-knowledge bar is the real risk. The company stack listed (Rust, Java/Spring, Scala, ClickHouse, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes, Terraform) overlaps almost nothing on his CV. No comp, no posted date, so freshness unconfirmed.

rows.title: Product Manager [IC4]
rows.location: Remote, globally distributed - EST and Europe preferred
rows.eligibility: Tier 1 - 'applicants from almost anywhere welcome if qualified', Europe named as a preferred zone, and comp is published per geographic zone which is how they actually hire outside the US; the binding condition is 20 hours/week of overlap with EST working hours, which is doable from Venice on an afternoon-into-evening shift
rows.comp: USD 167,200 (Zone 2) / USD 125,400 (Zone 3) / USD 83,600 (Zone 4) - Italy would fall in the lower zones
rows.posted: page metadata shows a 2025 date - likely older than 30 days; posting itself was live when fetched 2026-08-05
rows.why: One of very few PM postings that explicitly requires a prior engineering role or hands-on coding, which converts his lack of a PM title into an asset rather than a gap. Dev-tools and AI coding agents are a domain he uses daily (Claude Code is on his stack list), and the job is defined as organising customer feedback and pushing products from experimental to GA - close to his platform-migration ownership when he took a live product from Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel.
rows.watch_outs: 5+ years of product management is asked for and he has ~3 years with no PM title - the biggest stretch in this list. IC4 at a company with published levelling means the band is assessed formally. Zone-based pay could land near USD 83,600 for Italy. Metadata suggests the posting is not fresh, so confirm it is still being worked before investing in a tailored application.

rows.title: Technical Product Manager
rows.location: Remote, between PT and CET time zones
rows.eligibility: Tier 1 - CET is the far end of the stated hiring band and Venice is CET, so no permit or move is required; visa sponsorship is offered but only as an option for those who want to relocate to the US
rows.comp: not disclosed - 'competitive salary + equity + token pool'
rows.posted: not disclosed on posting (EU Greenhouse renders no date; live when fetched 2026-08-05)
rows.why: A genuine 0-to-1 product ownership role that states no years-of-experience requirement and explicitly says no programming is needed, which suits a candidate whose product credibility comes from shipping rather than from a PM career ladder. Defining developer-facing APIs and SDKs and going out to technical users to find friction is work he has done from the other side of the table, integrating Office RnD, Nexudus, Clubee and OpenAI APIs.
rows.watch_outs: The domain is decentralised ML training infrastructure and the posting calls a background in distributed systems, compute platforms or compilers essential - he cannot evidence any of those, and this is the row where the domain gap is widest. Crypto-adjacent, with part of the package in a token pool. No comp number and no posted date.

rows.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
rows.location: Remote, but must be based in London, UK or Dublin, Ireland
rows.eligibility: Tier 3 (Relocation + Sponsorship) - remote in name only: the posting requires residence in London or Dublin. His Italian EU long-term residence permit does not grant UK work rights, and Ireland opted out of the EU Long-Term Residence Directive, so Dublin needs an Irish employment permit. Listed because the role content is the closest match in the slice, not because the eligibility works today.
rows.posted: not disclosed on posting (Greenhouse renders no date; live when fetched 2026-08-05)
rows.why: Purely on responsibilities this is the best-matched posting the sweep found: lead POC workshops through to production, write and deploy Python/TypeScript/Node inside customer environments, build reusable reference implementations, and feed field insight back to product - with GenAI, CRM and CDP named explicitly. That is his FlowSpace and agency-facing work almost line for line, including the GTM/revenue-adjacent automation that is unusual on an engineer's CV.
rows.watch_outs: Relocation to London or Dublin plus a work permit, so slow and low-probability. Asks 5+ years hands-on software engineering against his ~3. Big-corporate with a long enterprise hiring loop, which his profile flags as a worse fit. Roughly 30% travel. Only worth pursuing if he is actively willing to move.
